transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to get our pre-lock round-robin started so we can move toward final production approval. Let's go through each area: technical, rights, talent, and accessibility leads — please report your final operating requirements. I'll make the binding production approval once I've heard from all four of you.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technical finding from my completed RF survey. Wireless roaming camera links interfere with the Orpheum Theater's assistive-listening loop. Because of that, the gala must use three fixed wired cameras from the marked camera platforms — no wireless roaming cameras. I filed the survey in the technical folder, but it's not on Mara's draft lock sheet yet, so I want to make sure everyone has this before we proceed.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical rights restriction. My signed performance license permits the gala broadcast but prohibits any video-on-demand release or later promotional clips. The recording must be marked broadcast-only. I received the countersigned license this morning and have not yet entered the restriction in the rights tracker, so I'm disclosing it now before we proceed to final approval. This directly conflicts with the current draft package's provision permitting the recording to be reused in the festival archive.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag two critical talent constraints from the headliner's agent that I confirmed by email but haven't yet entered into the production schedule. First, the headliner can soundcheck only at exactly 3:00 PM on Saturday — no other time slots are available. Second, the performer's rider explicitly prohibits sponsor product placement anywhere on the performance stage. This directly conflicts with the current draft package's provision that includes a sponsor product display on stage. Both constraints are confirmed in the agent's email to me.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical accessibility requirement from my caption vendor. The live caption feed requires the captioner to work from Booth B, whose dedicated return feed is connected to the gala's caption encoder. The general plan's control-room location will not work. I documented the vendor confirmation in the accessibility file, but I have not yet added the booth assignment to the lock sheet, so I'm disclosing it now before we proceed to final approval.
transcript.speaker: A5

decisions.camera_configuration: Three fixed wired cameras from the marked camera platforms; no wireless roaming cameras
decisions.archive_release: Broadcast-only; no video-on-demand release, no promotional clips, no reuse in the festival archive
decisions.stage_sponsor_treatment: No sponsor product placement anywhere on the performance stage; sponsor display must be relocated to a non-stage area or removed
decisions.captioner_location: Booth B, using its dedicated return feed connected to the gala's caption encoder

commitments.detail: Update the technical lock sheet to reflect three fixed wired cameras from marked camera platforms with no wireless roaming cameras, per the RF survey findings.
Enter the broadcast-only restriction in the rights tracker and remove the festival archive reuse provision from the draft package.
Enter the 3:00 PM Saturday soundcheck and the stage sponsor product placement prohibition into the production schedule.
Add the Booth B captioner assignment to the lock sheet and update the control-room plan accordingly.
Relocate the sponsor product display off the performance stage to a compliant non-stage location, or remove it entirely, before final lock.
